To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

abnormal findings in MRI images due to epidural injection using air were most frequently observed in MR images obtained within 3 days of injection, and that the incidence of abnormal findings was 82%.
the incidence of MRI abnormalities after ESI was 54% within 24 h, 31% within 48 h, and 25% within 72 h after the injection.
the most common abnormal MRI findings in patients who underwent an ESI were epidural air and fluid, which were observed in 41 and 31% of patients who had MRI within 3 and 2 days, respectively.

the effect of epidural cortico-steroid injection on magnetic reson-ance imaging findings.
the effect of epidural cortisone injection on magnetic resonance images (MRI).
the effects of epidural steroid injection on magnetic resonance images of the lumbar spinal cord.

MRI should be performed within 3 days of the injection.
epidural air, the needle tracks, and the soft tissue changes are the most frequent abnormal MRI findings after epidural injection at the lumbar region.
the use of air for the loss of resistance method should not be used for lumbar spine injections.

epidural corticosteroïd injections are a safe and effective treatment for low back pain and radicular pain.
the MRI changes after epidural corticosteroïd injection (ECI) are not permanent and are not related to the clinical outcome.
epidural steroid injections can lead to abnormal MRI findings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of abnormal MRI findings due to an epidural injection is time-dependent and that the presence of these findings should be considered when interpreting MR images of patients who have undergone an ESI.
MRI images obtained within 24 h or 2 to 3 days after epidural corticoid injection may be misinterpreted because of the presence of air or fluid within the epidural space.
MRI findings after an ESI should be interpreted carefully.
